# Background / Introduction

This notebook performs quality control and decontamination of viral sequencing data through several key steps:

1. Parsing technical metadata from FASTQ files, including:
   - Sequencing machine IDs
   - Flow cell IDs 
   - Run IDs

2. Removing potential contaminants by:
   - Applying batch-aware prevalence filters
   - Screening against a curated blacklist of common viral contaminants
   - Filtering low-abundance viral sequences

The goal is to generate a high-confidence set of viral counts for downstream analysis.

# Decontaminating Viral reads

## Parsing metadata from FASTQ files

```{r}
parse_header_info <- function(fastq_path, output_path){
    require(magrittr)
    require(dplyr)

    extract_headers <- function(fastq_path) {
        fastq_data <- ShortRead::readFastq(fastq_path)
        as.character(ShortRead::id(fastq_data))
    }

    summarize_header_info <- function(header_list){
        # Convert the character vector to a data frame first
        header_df <- stringr::str_split(header_list, ":") %>%
            purrr::map_dfr(~ data.frame(
                Instrument = .x[1],
                RunID = .x[2], 
                FlowCellID = .x[3]
            ))

        # Now we can use group_by since we have a data frame
        header_df %>%
            group_by(Instrument, RunID, FlowCellID) %>%
            janitor::get_dupes() %>%
            dplyr::distinct()
    }

    df <- extract_headers(fastq_path) %>% summarize_header_info()
    saveRDS(df, output_path)
}

batchtools_params <- list.files(
    glue("{pdmbs_dir}/workflow/RNASEQ/clean_reads"),
    pattern = "fastq.gz",
    full.names = TRUE
    ) %>% 
    data.frame("fastq_path" = .) %>%
    mutate(sample_id = basename(fastq_path) %>% strex::str_before_last("_")) %>%
    mutate(annot = case_when(
        grepl("_R1.fastq.gz", fastq_path) ~ "fwd",
        grepl("_R2.fastq.gz", fastq_path) ~ "rev",
        TRUE ~ "ERROR"
    )) %>%
    filter(file.size(fastq_path) > 100) %>% 
    mutate(output_path = file.path(
        header_summary_dir,
        paste0(
            tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(fastq_path), compression = TRUE),
            ".rds"
        )
    )) %>% 
    filter(!file.exists(output_path)) %>%
    select(fastq_path, output_path) %>%
    glimpse()

# configure registry ----
cluster_run <- glue("{get_time()}_ParseHeaders")
message("\n\nRUNNING: ", cluster_run, "\n")
breg <- makeRegistry(
    file.dir = glue(
        "{wkdir}/.cluster_runs/",
        cluster_run
    ),
    seed = 42
)
breg$cluster.functions <- batchtools::makeClusterFunctionsSlurm(
    template = glue("{wkdir}/batchtools_templates/batchtools.slurm.tmpl"),
    scheduler.latency = 0.1,
    fs.latency = 1
)

# Calculate chunks to get ~100 jobs
n_files <- length(batchtools_params$fastq_path)
chunk_size <- ceiling(n_files / 2000)

# Submit Jobs ----
jobs <- batchMap(
    fun = parse_header_info,
    args = batchtools_params,
    reg = breg
)
jobs[, chunk := chunk(job.id, chunk.size = chunk_size)]


submitJobs(jobs,
    resources = list(
        walltime = round(500 * chunk_size * 1.1), # 60 min per file
        memory = "200GB", # 50GB per job
        ncpus = 6,
        max.concurrent.jobs = 9999
    )
)

```

# Decontamination Pipeline

```{r}
# Abundance threshold ----
og_taxa <- microbiome::taxa(ps)

# Most abundant sample needs to have at least 10 reads
relab <- microbiome::abundances(ps)
taxa_count_maxs <- apply(relab, 1, max)
count_threshold <- (taxa_count_maxs >= 10)
ps_trim_abund <- ps %>% subset_taxa(count_threshold)
taxa_trimmed_abund <- og_taxa[!og_taxa %in% microbiome::taxa(ps_trim_abund)]

# Prevalence threshold ----
ps_trim_prev <- ps %>% 
    microbiome::core(detection = 0, prevalence = 0.01)
taxa_trimmed_prev <- og_taxa[
    !og_taxa %in% microbiome::taxa(ps_trim_prev)
    ]

# Lab reagent contaminants ----
# Read in the laboratory reagent contaminants
lab_reagent_contaminants <- read_csv(
    glue("{wkdir}/data/input/virome/",
        "total_raw_count_per_virus_id_in_laboratory_reagents.csv")
    ) %>%
    glimpse()

contaminant_ids <- lab_reagent_contaminants %>%
    filter(count > 5) %>%
    pull(virus) %>%
    unique()

```

## Batch effect analysis for sequencing instrument/flowcell

```{r}
calculate_batch_prevalence <- function(ps_obj, subset_var) {
  require(magrittr)
  subset_data <- microbiome::meta(ps_obj)[[subset_var]]
  batches <- subset_data %>% unique()
  prevalence_stats <- tibble::tibble()
  for (batch in batches) {
    print(batch)
    batch_samples <<- grepl(batch, subset_data)
    # skip if there are less than 25 samples in a batch
    if (sum(batch_samples) < 25) next
    ps_batch <- phyloseq::subset_samples(ps_obj, batch_samples)
    print(ps_batch)
    batch_stats <- microbiome::prevalence(ps_batch) %>%
      stack() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        batch_subset = as.character(batch),
        batch_variable = subset_var,
        sample_n = phyloseq::nsamples(ps_batch)
      )
    prevalence_stats %<>% dplyr::bind_rows(batch_stats)
  }
  return(prevalence_stats)
}

ps_groups <- c(
    "Case" = phyloseq::subset_samples(ps, case_control_other_latest == "Case"),
    "Control" = phyloseq::subset_samples(ps, case_control_other_latest == "Control"),
    "Other" = phyloseq::subset_samples(ps, case_control_other_latest == "Other")
)

# Define batch variables to analyze
batch_meta <- c("instrument_id", "flowcell_id")
# Create combinations for analysis
pair_combos <- expand_grid(
    ps_list = names(ps_groups),
    var_list = batch_meta
) %>%
    mutate(batch_id = glue("{ps_list}_{var_list}"))

# Run prevalence analysis
tic("Calculating batch prevalence")
prevalence_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
    list(
        ps = pair_combos$ps_list,
        var = pair_combos$var_list,
        id = pair_combos$batch_id
    ),
    function(ps, var, id) {
        result <- calculate_batch_prevalence(ps_groups[[ps]], var)
        if(!is.null(result)) {
            result$grouping_meta <- id
            return(result)
        }
    }
)
toc()

# Process prevalence statistics
prevalence_stats_proc <- prevalence_stats %>%
    filter(batch_subset != "FALSE") %>%
    filter(!grepl(";", batch_subset)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(batch_subset)) %>%
    mutate(case_control_other_latest = 
        strex::str_before_first(grouping_meta, "_")
    )

# Summarize prevalence statistics
prevalence_stat_summary <- prevalence_stats_proc %>%
    filter(sample_n >= 50) %>%
    get_dupes(ind, batch_variable, case_control_other_latest) %>%
    filter(dupe_count > 1) %>%
    group_by(ind, batch_variable, case_control_other_latest) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
        min = min(values),
        max = max(values),
        prevalence_delta = max - min,
        .groups = "drop"
    )

# Identify potential contaminants
blacklist_prev <- prevalence_stat_summary %>%
    filter(max > 0.5, min <= max / 2) %>%
    arrange(desc(prevalence_delta)) %>%
    pull(ind) %>%
    unique() %>% 
    as.character()

# Create visualization
plot_df <- prevalence_stat_summary %>%
    mutate(blacklist = ind %in% blacklist_prev) %>%
    arrange(blacklist, desc(prevalence_delta)) %>%
    mutate(ind = factor(ind))

# Generate plots
p1 <- plot_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = ind, y = prevalence_delta, color = blacklist)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_color_d3() +
    facet_grid(batch_variable ~ case_control_other_latest) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(x = "microbe", y = "max prevalence - min prevalence") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

p2 <- plot_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(
        x = case_control_other_latest,
        y = prevalence_delta,
        color = blacklist
    )) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_line(aes(group = ind), alpha = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~batch_variable, ncol = 1) +
    scale_color_d3() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = 'none')

# Combine and save plots
final_plot <- p1 + p2 + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))

ggsave(
    glue("{wkdir}/figures/Viral/",
    "decontamination-{Sys.Date()}_sequencing-batch_prevalence_filter.png"),
    final_plot,
    width = 16,
    height = 4
)

# Save results
saveRDS(
    prevalence_stats_proc,
    glue("{wkdir}/data/interim/PalmDB_mapping/decontamination/",
        "{Sys.Date()}_sequencing-batch_prevalence_stats.rds")
)

saveRDS(
    blacklist_prev,
    glue("{wkdir}/data/interim/PalmDB_mapping/decontamination/",
        "{Sys.Date()}_sequencing-batch_prevalence_blacklist.rds")
)

```

Visualize the relationship between virus prevalence and mean relative abundance

```{r}
prev_stats <- microbiome::prevalence(ps_trim) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    setNames("prev") %>%
    rownames_to_column("taxon") %>%
    glimpse()

rel_abund_df <- ps_trim %>% 
    microbiome::transform("compositional") %>% 
    microbiome::abundances() %>% 
    t() %>% 
    as.data.frame() %>% 
    glimpse()

taxon_iqr <- rel_abund_df %>%
    purrr::map(~IQR(., na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    unlist()

rel_abund_summary <- data.frame(
  taxon = colnames(rel_abund_df),
  prevalence = prev_stats$prev,
  mean = colMeans(rel_abund_df),
  ci95 = taxon_iqr) %>%
  glimpse()

# Get taxa annotations from phyloseq object
taxa_annots <- tax_table(ps_trim) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("taxon") %>%
    # Get finest resolution annotation (last non-NA value in each row)
    mutate(finest_annot = apply(., 1, function(x) {
        non_na <- x[!is.na(x)]
        if(length(non_na) > 1) {
            return(non_na[length(non_na)])
        } else {
            return(x[1]) # Return taxon ID if no other annotations
        }
    })) %>% 
    glimpse()

# Add annotations to abundance summary
rel_abund_summary %<>%
    left_join(taxa_annots %>% 
    select(taxon, finest_annot), by = "taxon") %>%
    mutate(is_top15 = rank(-mean) <= 100) %>% 
    glimpse()

# Create scatter plot with labels
p_abund_prev <- ggplot(rel_abund_summary, aes(x = prevalence, y = mean)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_text_repel(
        # data = subset(rel_abund_summary, is_top15),
        aes(label = finest_annot),
        size = 3,
        box.padding = 0.5,
        max.overlaps = Inf
    ) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("grey60", "red")) +
    labs(x = "Prevalence (Fraction of Samples)",
         y = "Mean Relative Abundance") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none"
    )
# p_abund_prev

ggsave(
    glue("{wkdir}/figures/Viral/",
        "Virus-prevalence-vs-mean-rel-abund_{Sys.Date()}.png"),
    p_abund_prev,
    width = 5, height = 4.5
)
```

```{r}
# remove taxa that are in every sample
oddly_abundant_taxa <- c("u101227", "u103829", "u110641")
# Remove taxa that are present in every sample
ps <- prune_taxa(!taxa_names(ps) %in% oddly_abundant_taxa, ps)

# meta(ps) %>% glimpse
abund_df <- abundances(ps) %>% as.data.frame()
colnames(abund_df)

# When dividing a dataframe by a vector, R performs element-wise division:
# - Each column in the dataframe is divided by the corresponding element in the vector
# - The vector is recycled if needed to match the dataframe dimensions
# - In this case, each sample's abundances are divided by that sample's total clean reads
total_clean_read_normmed <- sweep(abund_df, 2, meta(ps)$clean_read_counts_numeric, "/")

meta(ps) %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
    filter(sample_id == "PP-91097-BLM0T1") %>%
    pull(clean_read_counts_numeric)


# # Checking that normalization worked
# abund_df$`PP-91097-BLM0T1`
# # abund_df$`PP-91097-BLM0T1` / 33369892
# total_clean_read_normmed$`PP-91097-BLM0T1`


# Convert normalized matrix back to phyloseq object format
otu_table_norm <- otu_table(total_clean_read_normmed, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
# Replace abundance table in phyloseq object while keeping all other components
ps <- phyloseq(otu_table_norm, tax_table(ps), sample_data(ps))

saveRDS(
    ps,
    glue("{palm_interim}/",
        "phyloseq_count_matrix_BWA-dlist-GRCh38-dna-rna",
        "_decontaminated-outlier-removed-&_cleanread-normed_{Sys.Date()}.rds"
    )
)
```
